title: Daily Market Digest: July 29, 2026
subtitle: Market overview as of end-of-day, July 29, 2026

items.headline: U.S. Markets Close Mixed Amid Fed Decision and Tech Earnings
items.summary: U.S. equities saw a mixed close today as investors digested the Federal Reserve's latest interest rate decision and anticipated earnings reports from major tech companies. The Dow Jones Industrial Average posted solid gains, while the S&P 500 edged higher. Conversely, the Nasdaq Composite faced pressure, primarily from the semiconductor sector, which continued its recent downtrend. Overall market sentiment was a blend of cautious optimism from defensive sectors and ongoing concerns over AI investment returns.

items.headline: Bloom Energy Soars on Strong Q2 Results
items.summary: Shares of Bloom Energy ($BE) jumped 11% after the fuel cell maker reported record Q2 results, surpassing revenue and earnings expectations and raising its full-year outlook. This surge was primarily driven by accelerating demand from AI data centers and hyperscale customers.

items.headline: Coca-Cola Rallies After Raising Forecasts
items.summary: Coca-Cola ($KO) rallied 5.0% today after the beverage giant raised its annual revenue and profit forecasts, attributing strong performance partly to the FIFA World Cup.

items.headline: SanDisk Continues Slide Amid Market Pressures
items.summary: SanDisk ($SNDK) experienced a significant drop of 14.2%, extending its month-long decline. This movement is part of broader market pressures, particularly affecting the tech and semiconductor sectors.

items.headline: Micron Shares Fall as Chip Sector Weakens
items.summary: Micron ($MU) shares fell approximately 9% today, reflecting the continued pressure on semiconductor stocks. The broader Philadelphia Semiconductor Index tumbled 4.5%, driven by concerns over AI-related spending and chipmaking advancements.

items.headline: Federal Reserve Holds Rates Steady Amid Inflation Watch
items.summary: The Federal Reserve's Open Market Committee (FOMC) announced its decision to leave interest rates unchanged today, maintaining the target range at 3.5% to 3.75%. This marks the fifth consecutive meeting without a rate hike. While experts largely predicted this hold, rising oil prices have prompted increased speculation about potential rate hikes later in the year to combat persistent inflation.

items.headline: Big Tech Earnings Season Heats Up with Microsoft and Meta Reports
items.summary: Earnings season entered a critical phase today as tech giants Microsoft ($MSFT), Meta Platforms ($META), and Qualcomm ($QCOM) reported their quarterly results after market close. These reports are keenly watched by investors amidst heightened volatility and concerns over elevated valuations and aggressive spending on artificial intelligence infrastructure. Apple ($AAPL) and Amazon ($AMZN) are set to follow on Thursday.

items.headline: Defensive Sectors Lead as AI Spending Woes Weigh on Tech
items.summary: Today saw a notable rotation into defensive sectors, with healthcare jumping 2.4%, consumer staples gaining 2.0%, and materials advancing 1.7%. This shift comes as the technology sector, particularly chipmakers, continued to lag, with the S&P 500 technology index down 1.4%. Investors are increasingly concerned about whether massive investments in AI infrastructure will yield sufficient returns, a sentiment echoed by warnings from Fitch and Moody's regarding potential credit risks.
